title: Adaptations of life to cold, heat, dryness, salt and dim light (GEN.1725)
description: One row per adaptation of the table of docs/design/habitability/life-adaptations.md (from reports/life-adaptations-climate-2026-11-14.md): the climate it serves, the life that carries it, the axis whose limit it widens, the limit at the tolerant (grade 2) and extreme (grade 3) grades, the stage the life must have reached, and where it came from. The ordinary limit is one number for each axis (`axes`), so no two rows disagree about it. Every number is a stand-in of section 6.294 of docs/design/research/gap-filling-plan.md with its tier and tweak.

t_cold.basis: the freezing point of water: without an adaptation the life is active only above it (physics)

t_hot.basis: 40 C: the upper edge of ordinary (mesophilic) oxygen makers; a stand-in between the 30 to 37 C optimum of freshwater cyanobacteria and the thermophile mats

light_floor.basis: the middle of the older estimates of the minimum light for net growth, 0.3 to 5 umol m-2 s-1 (the measured floor is 0.04)

water_hours.basis: liquid water all year: a life with no tolerance of drying needs it

water_activity.basis: the water activity under which most ordinary cells stop dividing (the lowest at which any cell divides is 0.585)

ground_water_depth.basis: a water table within about 1 m reaches the surface by capillary rise and evaporation (extinction depth 0.3 to 1 m for deep-rooted cover)

insulation.basis: no cover: the ground is at the air's temperature

acid_strength.unit: percent of the liquid's mass that is sulfuric acid
acid_strength.basis: about pH 3 (a thousandth of a mole of acid a litre, 0.005 percent by mass): the acid under which most cells still divide; a stand-in (GEN.1811)

ammonia_fraction.unit: ammonia as a share of the water's mass
ammonia_fraction.basis: a tenth of a percent (0.06 M): the ammonia an ordinary cell takes as a nutrient and a trace; a stand-in under the 0.25 M a measured Halomonas grows in (GEN.1811)

cyanobacteria.basis: oxygen-making cyanobacteria by about 2.7 to 3.0 Ga on a life started at about 3.8 Ga (GEN.1724 LA8)

land_mats.basis: microbial mats on land by about 3.2 Ga (LA8)

animals.basis: no delay in GEN.1724: the animal stage of the life timeline decides

habitats.gate: liquid, lit, local temperature inside the life's cold and hot limits
liquid water under a lid of ice, the light that gets through it (ice_light.transmission) at or above the light floor
melt hours at or above the water-hours limit
liquid hours at or above the water-hours limit, local temperature at or above the cold limit
water table within the ground-water depth limit of the surface, or cut by relief (spring, oasis, playa)
habitats.production: refuge, or plant once rooted plants exist

habitats.gate: water activity at or above the water-activity limit
water at or under the hot limit

the medium of a chemical class that is not water at a habitable temperature: sulfuric acid (5a, 5b, 9), dense CO2 (6), a hydrocarbon sea (7), ammonia-water (8); read from the class gate (`life_classes`)

adaptations.name: shade adaptation under ice (more pigment, low light floor)
adaptations.note: grade 3 is the measured 0.04 umol m-2 s-1 (daily mean, under the Arctic pack); grade 2 is the geometric mean of the ordinary 1.0 and that, a straight guess

adaptations.name: plankton blooms under sea ice
adaptations.note: over 40 percent of the modelled Arctic production is in water with more than 85 percent ice cover

adaptations.name: mats under perennial lake ice
adaptations.note: year-round under 3 to 5 m of ice

adaptations.name: thin-ice refugia on a frozen-over world
adaptations.note: survived global glaciations where the ice was thin enough to admit light

adaptations.name: sea-ice brine-channel algae
adaptations.note: growth in brine at about -2 to -6 C, recalled

adaptations.name: snow algae with a carotenoid sunscreen
adaptations.note: microbes caused 17 percent of the melt of an Alaskan icefield

adaptations.name: cryoconite holes (dark mats melt pits into the ice)
adaptations.note: photosynthesis 2.9 times respiration with water seldom above 0.1 C; all holes on Earth about 5e-4 of Earth's burial

adaptations.name: lichen photosynthesis while frozen or nearly so
adaptations.note: carbon-14 fixation confirmed at -10.9 C (grade 2); field activity as low as -20 C (grade 3); range -24 C (laboratory) to -17 C

adaptations.name: rock-hidden (cryptoendolith) communities
adaptations.note: active only above freezing and wet; carbon turnover about 20,000 years

adaptations.name: moss banks and carpets (the ice blanket)
adaptations.note: grow where the mean year is -4.8 C; bank depth and age recalled; the insulation in kelvin is not sourced

adaptations.name: snow cover as insulation
adaptations.effect_on_habitat: ground under deep snow stays near 0 to -5 C while the air is far colder
adaptations.note: physical, recalled

adaptations.name: photosynthesis under thin snow
adaptations.note: lengthens the season by days to weeks, recalled

adaptations.name: cushion and rosette form
adaptations.effect_on_habitat: the plant runs several degrees above the air; soil under cushions differs by up to about 15 C
adaptations.note: the up-to-15 C is a maximum, not a typical value

adaptations.name: antifreeze and ice-binding proteins
adaptations.note: lowers the freezing point by about 1 to 2 C in fish blood; recalled

adaptations.name: freeze tolerance (sugar or glycerol cryoprotectants)
adaptations.note: wood frog survives 65 to 70 percent of its body water frozen at -3 to -6 C; dormant while frozen, so it moves no activity limit

adaptations.name: cold-active enzymes and membranes (psychrophily)
adaptations.note: bacterial growth to about -15 C, activity to about -25 C in permafrost brine; a microbe of water, carried by the water classes 3a to 4c (GEN.1811)

adaptations.name: thermophilic cyanobacterial mats
adaptations.note: mats at 53 to 63 C (grade 2 is 60 C); the limit for oxygen-making cells is about 73 to 75 C (346 to 348 K)

adaptations.name: acid hot-spring red algae (Cyanidium type)
adaptations.note: to about 56 to 57 C at pH 0.5 to 3, recalled

adaptations.name: hyperthermophily
adaptations.note: growth to 122 C (optimum 98 C); a microbe of water, carried by the water classes 3a to 4c (GEN.1811)

adaptations.name: heat-shock proteins (chaperones)
adaptations.note: survive brief heat a few to ten degrees above the growth limit; moves no steady limit

adaptations.name: fast heat acclimation of photosynthesis
adaptations.note: Tidestromia thrives above 45 C and raises its photosynthesis optimum within a day; land plants stop near 47 to 50 C

adaptations.name: reflective hairs and waxes
adaptations.note: plants: less light used, so lower production

adaptations.name: behavioural timing (short safe forage window, burrow, nocturnal)
adaptations.note: lets animals live where the surface passes their limit

adaptations.name: hot-vent animals
adaptations.note: about 50 C is the highest known for animals, recalled

adaptations.name: biological soil crusts (cyanobacteria, lichens, mosses)
adaptations.note: wake only with liquid water, light and warmth together; cryptogamic covers fix about 7 percent of land production

adaptations.name: hypoliths under translucent stones
adaptations.note: down to about 5 mm of rain a year and 75 h a year of liquid water; falls about five orders of magnitude for a tenfold drop in rain

adaptations.name: halite endoliths (water drawn from the air by salt)
adaptations.note: lives where rain is under 1 mm a year; the hours are the GEN.1722 floor, not a measurement of the salt's own hours

adaptations.name: desiccation tolerance (anhydrobiosis, resurrection plants)
adaptations.note: survive near-total drying for years and revive on wetting; dormant, so it moves no activity limit

adaptations.name: CAM (pores open at night)
adaptations.note: far less water lost per carbon; a lower top rate than C3 or C4

adaptations.name: C4 (carbon pump)
adaptations.note: about 3 percent of plant species and about 23 percent of land carbon fixation; needs low carbon dioxide

adaptations.name: deep roots to groundwater (phreatophytes)
adaptations.note: desert mean maximum rooting depth 9.5 m, record 68 m; widens the seep from a table within 1 m to one within rooting depth

adaptations.name: dormancy and seed or spore banks
adaptations.note: wait out dry years

adaptations.name: compatible solutes (glycerol, betaine)
adaptations.note: oxygen-making algae (Dunaliella) live in brine near water activity 0.75; any life to 0.585 (not oxygen makers)

adaptations.name: far-red pigments (chlorophyll d and f)
adaptations.note: use light out to about 750 nm in shade; already class 1c

adaptations.name: deep red seaweeds
adaptations.note: fix carbon at a tiny fraction of a percent of surface light, recalled

adaptations.name: retinal light pumps
adaptations.note: energy, not oxygen (GEN.881)

adaptations.name: metabolism in the cold of a brine (Planococcus type)
adaptations.note: respiration of labelled substrate to -25 C (248.15 K) in permafrost brine, a heterotroph, not a chemolithotroph, so it stands for the cold edge of a chemical life (Marginal); the measured growth edge, -15 C, is C16's

adaptations.name: acid tolerance of the Picrophilus type
adaptations.note: grade 2 is growth around pH 0 (1 M of hydrogen ions, 0.5 M or 4.7 percent sulfuric acid, R5327); grade 3 is Picrophilus torridus adapted to 1.2 M sulfuric acid, 11 percent by mass (R5326; the percent is arithmetic over a density of 1.07). The classes sit at 81 percent and above: past the table, and the record says so

adaptations.name: ammonia tolerance of a Halomonas
adaptations.note: grade 3 is growth directly in 0.25 M ammonia (pH 10.18), 0.43 percent of the water's mass (R5328; none at 0.5 M); grade 2 is the geometric mean of it and the ordinary 0.1 percent, a straight guess. The class asks for 10 percent: 25 times the measured limit, past the table, and the record says so
